Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class SwingCompositedWindowSink

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.SwingCompositedWindowSink
All Implemented Interfaces:
CompositedWindowSink
public final class SwingCompositedWindowSink extends Object implements CompositedWindowSink
The 2D CompositedWindowSink: paints a redirected client window's pixels into a Swing component that the conventional 2D desktop can host inside a Desktop2DWindow, so a native X11 application appears within the desktop rather than escaping as a separate top-level window.

It keeps a full-window BufferedImage canvas. Each present(java.awt.image.BufferedImage, int, int, int, int) blits the freshly-read damage region into the canvas at its window-relative offset and repaints only that rectangle; resized(int, int) reallocates the canvas. The canvas is the single source the component paints, so the class needs no live gnu.x11.Display and no Java 3D and is fully unit-testable headlessly (the blit is a plain Graphics2D memory copy and a JPanel constructs under java.awt.headless=true).

Threading

present(java.awt.image.BufferedImage, int, int, int, int) runs on the window-manager event thread. The blit is performed under a lock shared with JComponent.paintComponent(java.awt.Graphics) so the canvas is never painted mid-copy; only the cheap repaint() is marshalled to the EDT (Swing's repaint() is itself thread-safe, but the dirty rectangle is queued explicitly for clarity).
